independent.summary: The new docs paragraph opens with a blanket contract — "Any route taking an id in its path … answers 400 {"error":"INVALID_ID"} … when that parameter is not a valid 24-hex ObjectId" — that two id routers do not honor: `PUT/DELETE /relationship-types/:id` (server/src/routes/relationshipTypes.js:62,85) still throws a CastError into `catch (err) { res.status(500).json({ error: err.message }) }` and answers 500 with the driver's cast text, and `/entity-types/:id` (server/src/routes/entityTypes.js:111 `findOwn`) answers 404, not 400 INVALID_ID. The sentence that follows names the six registered routers, and kol_emet_spec.md admits relationship-types is still open, so the code is in scope — but the published contract now documents behavior the API does not have for every `:id` route.
